`428209 (2006 VC)` exceeds the radiation momentum ceiling (eps = 1.28) with a reliable orbit solution and is not in the channel's explained set.

A2 = 6.4e-13 au/day^2, S/N 3.8, arc 7139.0 d, diameter 341 m (from H).

Next step is `loom-litcheck --name "428209 (2006 VC)"`: the dark-comet population is incomplete and most exceedances resolve to it.

active.body:
`loom` has advanced from MJD 61353.32603 to MJD 61359.23043 — 5.9 days of sky — after sitting still since 2026-11-10T00:27:12Z.

The stall was confirmed across 7.0 days of sightings; the advance itself happened between 2026-11-16T23:22:56Z and now, so the interval between successive frontier values is 7.0 days. That is an UPPER BOUND on the mirror's true ingest gap — this repository samples the frontier about once a day and cannot see a change finer than that.

The frontier is now 1.8 days behind the wall clock, inside the 30-day limit, so the age alert clears. That is not the same as current: the mirror's ordinary lag is ~16 days, and anything above that is still backlog.

This is the cadence datum `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` has never had — it was set to 7 by guesswork because no advance had ever been observed here. Recalibrate it against `observed_advance_days` in `results/alerts/frontier.json` now that there is one.

Note that the nights lost to the stall are ABSENT, not null: they were never observed, so they add nothing to the screen's trial count and must not be counted as clean sky.
active.title: LOOM's data frontier is moving again (+5.9 days of sky)

active.body:
GitHub's scheduler did not start `tocsin.yml` at its scheduled firing of 2026-11-16T14:10:00Z (cron `10 14 * * *`, cadence 24.0 h), and it is now 8.34 h past that slot. Its last scheduled run was 2026-11-15T19:41:16Z.

Automatic recovery has not established a successful execution. This is one unresolved incident; later missed slots will not generate another notification.

NO catch-up was dispatched (the dispatch was not attempted).

Scheduled runs on GitHub are best effort and are dropped under load. A dropped firing leaves no failed run for the watchdog to retry and no stale result until the staleness window expires days later, which is why it is watched separately.
active.title: tocsin did not fire at 2026-11-16T14:10:00Z

active.body:
The `asassn` adapter reached its service but has no usable path to a light curve.

Reason recorded by the probe: no cone request was accepted (every variant and format in the matrix above), and the vendor client cannot be imported here -- so there is no path to a light curve, only to metadata

A screen over this feed would run, commit and report nothing found -- which is indistinguishable from a quiet sky and is not a result. Read `results/tocsin_altfeeds/probe.json`; the request matrix there records responses and connection errors.
active.title: ASASSN cannot serve light curves
